question: what is the -38 dBFS floor, and can the recalibration run in this room at all
reading: Covering the microphone did not lower the floor (-38.05 -> -36.29, slightly higher), so this is not room noise. Touching the microphone adds contact noise, which can mask an acoustic drop, so the test is suggestive rather than conclusive.

There is no DC offset (-66.9 dBFS) and no single mains line: the strongest bins below 2 kHz are spread from 6 Hz to 51 Hz at -51 to -55 dBFS each, and 43% of the energy sits between 300 and 5000 Hz. So it is broadband, not hum.
A broadband floor that the hand does not reduce points at the input chain (preamp/codec) or at structure-borne coupling, not at the room.

With the source at -19.3 dBFS RMS the microphone only reaches -32.42 dBFS, i.e. 5.6 dB above the floor. To reach 20 dB of excitation-to-noise the source would have to run near -5 dBFS RMS, which is 21 dB louder than B's calibration level and well into the region B flagged as non-linear.

options.A: raise the excitation to about -5 dBFS RMS - direct, but B must accept the non-linearity
options.B: get the input floor down (different input gain stage, shielded/balanced cabling, away from switching supplies) - keeps B's level, needs a hardware change
options.C: accept the floor and document that the open-loop refit cannot be done in this setup - honest but leaves one-click recalibration unproven

not_claimed: the floor source is not yet positively identified; the hand-cover test is not clean because contact noise was added.
hand_covered_conclusion: covering the microphone RAISES the level (uncovered -38.05, covered -34.00 / -35.63 / -32.18), because contact and handling noise exceed whatever acoustic noise it blocks. The hand test therefore cannot isolate the floor, but it does rule out a room-acoustic-dominated floor: blocking the port would have dropped that by far more than it rose.
status: the floor is in the input chain (preamp/codec/cabling) or structure-borne; at B level the excitation reaches only 5.6 dB above it.
